name: Alternating Incline Dumbbell Press
description: The Alternating Incline Dumbbell Press is performed on an incline bench (30-45 degrees), targeting the clavicular head of the pectoralis major, with one arm pressing while the other holds the dumbbell in a fixed position near the upper chest. This anti-rotation, unilateral loading approach builds upper chest strength alongside core stability.

execution.starting_position: Set bench to 30-45 degrees. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at upper chest level. Both elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust bench angle. Set up the same as an alternating flat dumbbell press but on the incline.
steps: Step 1: Press one dumbbell upward from upper chest to full lockout.
Step 2: Return that arm to the starting position.
Step 3: Press the other arm while holding the first at chest level.
Step 4: Alternate for all prescribed reps.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as each arm presses. Inhale as it returns.
common_mistakes: Steep angle (>45°) turning the movement into a shoulder press
Torso rotation toward the pressing arm
safety_considerations: Keep the stationary dumbbell secure — do not let it drift
Use a lighter load than bilateral incline press
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension per arm. Stationary arm at 90 degrees of elbow flexion.
coaching_cues: Hips and shoulders stay square to the ceiling
The resting arm is under constant isometric load — treat it seriously
